reasoning.text: The render now passes both acceptance tests and closes all three carried-over gaps: TOP shows all eight blue BRAM banks, eight copper DSP multipliers as a clean orange column, the symmetric add/sub clusters, the two distinct reduction members (cylindrical Barrett spine + boxy shift/subtract), the right-edge controllers and both white FIFOs; FRONT/ISO show the exploded butterfly lane on its two risers and the seven-fin exploded heatsink, and the return bus carries a clear arrowhead into the crossbar. The remaining weakness is a dataflow asymmetry: only the operand-return path is drawn as a visible bus, so the twiddle-broadcast and crossbar-read paths are inferable only from the connection graph, not from the silhouette. A second nit is that adder and subtractor members are materially identical, so a viewer cannot tell sum from difference at a glance even though the build test wants them labelled.
gaps: Draw the crossbar-read path as a third visible bus (crossbar -> multiplier column inputs) to complete the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad; right now only twiddle and return are rendered, so the operand-read half of the conflict-free RMW loop is still invisible in ISO.

Give the eight subtractor members a distinct material (e.g. brushed steel vs the adders' dark anodized aluminum) so sum vs difference is readable at a glance without losing the 'symmetric pair' grouping.
Consider nudging the exploded butterfly baseplate +Z by ~1.2 m so it no longer sits directly over its source lane in the TOP plan view, where it currently occludes lanes 2-4.

fields.before: On-chip ROM storing precomputed roots of unity, reused across the rearranged loop so each factor is fetched once and broadcast to all eight multipliers.
fields.after: On-chip ROM storing precomputed roots of unity, reused across the rearranged loop so each factor is fetched once and broadcast over the feeder/rail to all eight multipliers.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Lay one shared open butterfly-array baseplate across the array, then populate it with eight parallel butterfly clusters (one per BRAM bank); inside each cluster wire the DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder and subtractor, then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar, capped with a return arrow at the crossbar end to close the conflict-free read-modify-write loop. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM (feeding all multipliers), the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), and clamp the seven-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
meta.after: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Lay one shared open butterfly-array baseplate across the array, then populate it with eight parallel butterfly clusters (one per BRAM bank); inside each cluster wire the DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder and subtractor, then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar, capped with a return arrow at the crossbar end to close the conflict-free read-modify-write loop. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the rail spanning the multiplier column so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), and clamp the seven-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
